"""Split-word detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 2176.

What it does: it counts how many tokens so far make up the current word. A token continues
the word when it has no leading space, starts with a letter, and follows a token that ends
in a letter (a new document always starts a new word). The program predicts:
  - about +0.35 on the second piece of a word the tokenizer split into pieces
    (e.g. "of|acial", "so|ff|its", "dom|o|ic", "a|ther|ogenic"),
  - about +0.1 on the third piece,
  - 0 on the first piece of a word, on whole words, and on later pieces.

Why: the component's output direction promotes word-completion pieces (logit lens: "idges",
"ancies", "agents"), and it is most active while the model is partway through spelling a
word that is split across tokens.

Limits: this explains only about 3% of its variance. Most of the activation is dense, signed
and context dependent, and no token, bigram, script, position or word-frequency feature I
tried captured it. The word-piece rule is the simplest part that does.
"""

READS = ()

PIECE_VALUE = {2: 0.35, 3: 0.1}  # predicted activation by the word's piece number


def _continues_word(tok, prev):
    """Whether `tok` continues the current word: letter-initial with no leading space, after
    a token that ends in a letter. `prev` is empty at a document's start."""
    return bool(tok) and tok[0].isalpha() and bool(prev) and prev[-1].isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = "" if new_doc else prefix.token_strings[-2]
    pieces = carry or 0  # pieces of the current word so far
    pieces = pieces + 1 if pieces and _continues_word(tok, prev) else 1
    return pieces, PIECE_VALUE.get(pieces, 0.0)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 2177 (through component 2177 of down_proj).

The component reads one MLP hidden unit, number 2177 of layer 15, and writes it back
along a fixed direction. Its activation is about 0.88 times that unit's value (the unit
alone carries about half the activation's variance), so this program predicts the
activation from the word at the current position.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Adjectives about harm, usefulness or ability ("dangerous", "effective", "taxable",
  "profitable", "harmful") and Japanese ability forms ("できる", "になる") give a large
  positive value. These are the strongest positive contexts we saw.
- Words ending in -able, -ible, -ive give a moderate positive value; -ing words a small one.
- Past participles ending in -ed give a small negative value.
- Everything else sits at the average, about -0.07.

This explains only a little of the variance: word identity alone is weak for this unit,
and the same word can be high or low depending on its context.
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

HARM_OR_USE = {
    "dangerous", "harmful", "hazardous", "fatal", "deadly", "lethal", "toxic", "risky",
    "injurious", "disruptive", "damaging", "profitable", "taxable", "useful", "effective",
    "eligible", "relevant", "beneficial", "therapeutic", "medicinal", "valuable",
    "important", "critical", "influential", "productive", "qualifying", "controversial",
}
ABILITY_JA = {"できる", "出来る", "になる", "やすい", "える", "れる", "られる", "せる"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if word in HARM_OR_USE or prefix.token_strings[-1].strip() in ABILITY_JA:
        value = 2.0
    elif re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+(able|ible|ive)", word):
        value = 0.3
    elif re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]+ing", word):
        value = 0.14
    elif re.fullmatch(r"[a-z]{3,}ed", word):
        value = -0.12
    else:
        value = -0.07
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 2178 (down_proj component 2178), predicted as zero.

The component reads almost only that MLP hidden unit (its input weight is 0.85 on the unit
and at most 0.04 on any other), so its activation is that unit's value times about 1.
The value is dense (sd about 0.4) and has no readable trigger: the current token, the
previous token and position explain nothing held out, and the value is only weakly
correlated from one token to the next. It is largest inside random-looking base64 strings,
but there its sign is unpredictable. Predicting zero everywhere is the least-squares answer
when the sign is unknown.
"""

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 2179 (read out through down_proj component 2179).

What it does: this component is almost entirely MLP hidden unit 2179 of layer 15
(about 60% of its read-out vector sits on that one unit). Its activation is mostly a
small, diffuse number, but it is pushed clearly negative on the current token when the
token is a hedge, negation or "it depends" qualifier ("not", "non-", "perhaps", "maybe",
"may", "necessarily", "unless", "rather", "instead") or a word about variety and
flexibility ("complex", "multiple", "diverse", "variety", "flexible", "dynamic").
Everywhere else it sits near a small negative baseline.

This program predicts that: -0.33 on those words, -0.03 elsewhere. It explains only a
sliver of the variance (the activation is mostly fine-grained context that no word list
captures), and it is a readable approximation, not a full model of the unit.
"""

READS = ()

HEDGE_OR_NEGATION = {
    "not", "non", "perhaps", "maybe", "may", "might", "possibly", "probably",
    "plausible", "necessarily", "unless", "rather", "instead",
}
VARIETY = {
    "complex", "complicated", "complexities", "multiple", "multi", "diverse",
    "diversity", "variety", "varied", "vary", "varies", "flexible", "flexibility",
    "dynamic", "heterogeneous", "irregular", "ongoing",
}
QUALIFIERS = HEDGE_OR_NEGATION | VARIETY
ON_QUALIFIER = -0.33
BASELINE = -0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the component's activation at the newest token."""
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    value = ON_QUALIFIER if word in QUALIFIERS else BASELINE
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15, MLP down_proj, component 2180: a near-silent, unexplained component.

What it does, as far as we can tell:
- It is (almost) never important to the model. Its causal importance is ~0 on every
  token, and switching it off changes the model's next-token predictions by ~nothing.
- Its activation (its contribution's size along U_c) is noise-like, with mean about -0.02
  and spread about 0.3. Nothing simple predicts it: the token's identity, its character
  class, the previous token, and a running average of earlier activity each explain
  under 2% of its variance on held-out text.
- The one clear regularity: at the first token a model sees in a row or a document (the
  position where attention has nothing before it), the activation is ~0 (std 0.003).
- Its input direction is mostly one MLP hidden unit of layer 15 (unit 2180, about 28% of
  the direction's squared norm), so its activation tracks that unit's value (r about 0.49).
  That unit's value is not something a token-level rule reproduces: the concept sets we
  tried (print/log/output calls, character classes, repeated tokens, bigrams) explain ~0.

So the program predicts 0 at the start of each document and the typical value
(about -0.02) everywhere else. It is a baseline, not an explanation of a mechanism.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL = -0.02  # the component's mean activation away from document starts


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # A new document starts at the row's first token and wherever the document label changes.
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    starts = prefix.position == 0 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return None, 0.0 if starts else TYPICAL

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 2181, read through its down_proj component, in plain terms.

The component reads almost only one MLP hidden unit (layer 15, unit 2181): its input
direction is that unit alone, plus a diffuse tail. So its activation is that unit's
value times the size of its output column. The unit is quiet almost everywhere
(typical value near 0.02). It spikes in maths word problems:

* Positive, on the tokens of an algebra drill sentence that starts with "Suppose" and
  contains an equation (e.g. "Suppose -3*n - 5 = 2*n + 10").
* Negative, on the word that opens a question sentence in a word problem
  ("How many ...", "What is ...", "Find ...", "Determine ...").

Everywhere else the program predicts the typical small value, 0.02.

This explains almost none of the variance (about 0.4% on training rows, about zero on
eval). Most of the activation is small, diffuse, and not tied to any token identity or
sentence type; the spikes are rare and their sign is not predictable from these rules.

The program splits text into sentences as it reads: a sentence ends at . ? ! or a
newline, and a document boundary starts a new one. The carry is the text of the
current sentence so far.
"""

import re

QUESTION_OPENERS = re.compile(
    r"(What|How|Find|find|Determine|Calculate|Which|Compute|Describe|Explain|Who|Where|When|Why)\b"
)
SUPPOSE_EQUATION = re.compile(r"Suppose\b.*(=|\d)", re.S)
SENTENCE_END = re.compile(r"[.?!]\s*$")

SUPPOSE_VALUE = 1.1  # mean activation on tokens of "Suppose ... = ..." sentences
OPENER_VALUE = -0.6  # mean activation on a question sentence's opening word
QUESTION_VALUE = -0.09  # mean activation on the rest of a question sentence
ELSEWHERE_VALUE = 0.02  # the component's typical small value everywhere else

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    sentence = "" if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    if SENTENCE_END.search(sentence) or sentence.endswith("\n"):
        sentence = ""
    before = sentence.lstrip()
    sentence = sentence + token
    text = sentence.lstrip()
    if SUPPOSE_EQUATION.match(text):
        value = SUPPOSE_VALUE
    elif QUESTION_OPENERS.match(text):
        opens_here = not QUESTION_OPENERS.match(before)
        value = OPENER_VALUE if opens_here else QUESTION_VALUE
    else:
        value = ELSEWHERE_VALUE
    return sentence, value

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:2182 (Qwen3-1.7B).

What it is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP down projection. Its input direction
(V) is dominated by one MLP hidden unit, 2182 (weight 0.42 of a unit-norm vector), so
its activation is roughly 0.37 times that hidden unit's value plus small terms from
about fifty others.

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical activation. The
component is nearly silent in the model: its causal importance is about 1e-7 and it
never passes the harvest threshold. Its activation is zero at the first token of each
document and otherwise centred near -0.018, with large context-driven swings
(std 0.30). We tried token identity, the previous token, token category (letters,
digits, punctuation, code-like, Han), position in the document, and document-level
means. None explains more than about 2 to 3 percent of the variance out of sample.
So the program predicts the mean, and zero at document starts.

Read it as "no short rule found": the program explains the component's mean level and
its inactivity, not its moment-to-moment variation.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.018  # mean over training text, away from document starts


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Zero at the first token of a document, otherwise the mean activation."""
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    starts_document = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if starts_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 2183, read through down_proj's component 2183.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of layers.15.mlp.down_proj. Its activation is
almost exactly the layer-15 MLP hidden unit 2183 (the unit's value times about 0.65), so
it is a signed, dense signal with std 0.38 and most of its mass at |x| between 0.1 and 1.

What we found: no simple token property carries it. Token identity explains under 1% of
its variance on held-out text, bigrams and token categories explain nothing, and a running
count of device or software words in the document explains nothing. Its mean is a little
above zero on device, computing and internet-UI words (phone, computer, software, database,
website, menu, file), roughly +0.1 to +0.8 on average, with a spread far larger than that.

What this program does: predicts +0.1 on those device and computing words and 0 on every
other token. It is the most readable thing the data supports; it explains only a sliver
of the variance, and a token-table or context model would add little that is readable.
"""

READS = ()

# Device, computing and internet-UI words, the vocabulary where the component leans positive.
DEVICE_WORDS = frozenset(
    """
    computer computers software hardware device devices phone phones mobile smartphone
    app apps program programs database online website web page internet email
    profile screen window box menu button settings file files folder digital camera
    click enter save code system server network login logged account browser
    download upload laptop tablet keyboard monitor printer electronic electric
    """.split()
)

# Mean activation of the device words on held-out text, about +0.1 on average.
DEVICE_VALUE = 0.1


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    return carry, (DEVICE_VALUE if word in DEVICE_WORDS else 0.0)

"""Copy-run detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj, component 2184.

In plain terms: this component goes negative while the text is copying earlier text
verbatim. A token counts as "copied" when it continues a span that already appeared
earlier in the same document, the way a repeated line, identifier or phrase does. The
longer the copied run so far, the more negative it gets. It is stronger in documents
where much of the text so far has been copied (templated logs, repeated code, lists),
and stronger on words than on punctuation or whitespace. Outside copied text it is
close to zero.

The program keeps, per document:
  run  - how many tokens in a row have continued the copy of the most recent earlier
         occurrence of the text (0 when the current token is not a copy)
  frac - the share of earlier tokens in this document that sat in a copy run of 3 or more

and predicts  -min(run - 1, 6) * (frac + 0.1) * weight, where weight is 1.5 for a word
token, 0.1 for whitespace and 0.8 for anything else. Nothing else is used.
"""

READS = ()

CAP = 6  # copy runs longer than this stop adding strength
FLOOR = 0.1  # strength for documents with no copying yet
MIN_COPY_RUN = 3  # a run this long counts toward a document's copied share


def word_weight(text):
    if text.strip() == "":
        return 0.1
    if text.strip().isalpha():
        return 1.5
    return 0.8


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    tokens = prefix.token_ids
    token = tokens[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "last": {}, "pointer": None, "run": 0, "seen": 0, "copied": 0}
    # Continue the copy if the token after the pointer matches this token,
    # otherwise restart the copy from the latest earlier occurrence of this token.
    pointer = carry["pointer"]
    if pointer is not None and pointer + 1 < t and tokens[pointer + 1] == token:
        carry["run"] += 1
        carry["pointer"] = pointer + 1
    elif token in carry["last"]:
        carry["pointer"] = carry["last"][token]
        carry["run"] = 1
    else:
        carry["pointer"] = None
        carry["run"] = 0
    run = carry["run"]
    frac = carry["copied"] / carry["seen"] if carry["seen"] else 0.0
    carry["last"][token] = t
    carry["seen"] += 1
    carry["copied"] += run >= MIN_COPY_RUN
    strength = min(max(run - 1, 0), CAP) * (frac + FLOOR)
    value = -strength * word_weight(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2185: a weak "separator right after a number" detector.

What it does: it is switched on at a token that is not a digit but directly follows a
digit inside the same document, the way the comma, period, hyphen, colon, space or
newline inside "1,000", "570 F.3d 75", "(571) 270-3948" or "10:30" does. Everywhere else
it sits near zero.

The activation is signed and heavy-tailed. On these positions it is positive about as
often as negative, and its large values come from mixed contexts (citations, code line
numbers, phone numbers, forum counts), so no token rule predicts its sign. The program
therefore predicts only the average value on those positions, about 0.3.
"""

READS = ()

POST_DIGIT_VALUE = 0.3


def _is_digit(text):
    return len(text) == 1 and text.isdigit()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return carry, 0.0
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    cur, prev = prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if _is_digit(prev) and not _is_digit(cur):
        return carry, POST_DIGIT_VALUE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Position-in-document rule for the component's activation.

The component (layers.15 MLP down_proj, unit 2186) has no readable trigger: its
activation is a diffuse, sign-symmetric value with std ~0.3, and nothing a token-level
program can name predicts it. The one stable pattern is where a document starts: the
first token of each document reads exactly 0, and the next few tokens sit slightly below
zero before the activation averages out to 0 again. This program predicts those means
by position within the document, and 0 otherwise.
"""
READS = ()

# mean activation at document position 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (training text); 0 after that
START_MEANS = (0.0, -0.084, -0.085, -0.053, -0.025)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    k = 0 if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1] + 1
    value = START_MEANS[k] if k < len(START_MEANS) else 0.0
    return (doc, k), value

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 2187 (the component's input direction is ~60% this unit).

What it does: nothing it can name. Its activation is a dense, signed value (std ~0.5, heavy
tails, near 0 at a document's first token), but none of the simple readings tried explain it:
the current token (holdout R^2 ~ 0), the previous token, token category (script, digits,
punctuation, spaces), position in the document, a ridge fit on hashed recent-token bags
(R^2 ~ 0.4%), or a recent-keyword rule (manage/despite/remarkable/while...; R^2 ~ 0.04%).
So the program predicts the mean, 0, at every position.

This is an honest null: it reproduces "switched off" to within rounding, and explains
almost none of the variance. A lookup table of token means would not do better.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Predict the component's activation at this position: 0, its mean."""
    return carry, 0.0

"""Verdicts negative, title dashes positive.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:2188 is quiet almost everywhere, and its
size is spread thinly over ordinary text. Its clearest moves are:
- negative, on a word that gives a verdict or opens a reply ("Hmm", "Great", "Good", "Perfect",
  "Nice", "Okay", "Not", "No", "Correct"), most strongly when the word starts a sentence;
- positive, on a dash that follows the name at the start of a document, as in an encyclopedia
  stub ("Albert Allard — ...").
Everywhere else it predicts 0.
"""

READS = ()

# Verdict and reply-opening words, with their typical activation at the start of a sentence.
VERDICT = {
    "hmm": -3.5, "great": -6.0, "perfect": -5.0, "excellent": -5.0, "nice": -6.0,
    "awesome": -6.0, "good": -4.0, "okay": -3.0, "fantastic": -2.0, "helpful": -1.5,
    "thanks": -1.5, "not": -2.5, "no": -1.0, "correct": -2.0, "invalid": -3.0,
    "exactly": -2.0, "yeah": -2.0, "error": -1.0, "failed": -1.0, "poor": -1.5,
}
SENTENCE_END = (".", "!", "?", "。", "！", "？", '"', "-", "*", "#")
DASHES = ("—", "–")


def opens_sentence(prefix):
    """True if the newest token starts a sentence: the first token of a document, or one that
    follows a sentence end, a line break, or an opening quote, dash or bullet."""
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return True
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    return "\n" in before or before.strip() == "" or before.strip() in SENTENCE_END


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: the newest token's place in its document (0 for a document's first token)
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry + 1
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    value = VERDICT.get(text.lower(), 0.0)
    if value and not opens_sentence(prefix):
        value /= 4  # mid-sentence, the same words barely move it
    if text in DASHES and pos <= 8:
        value = 4.0  # a dash just after the title at the start of a document
    return pos, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP component 2189, read as a concept detector for the words of structured
fact lists. Its input direction is mostly MLP hidden unit 2189 of layer 15 (about 70% of
its squared norm), so it tracks that unit's activation, which is diffuse: most of its
variance is not explained by any word list. The program keeps the part that is.

It is strongly negative on the field name "country" when it labels a field in a list of
facts ("Karkowka, country, Poland", "X -> country of citizenship ->"), and moderately
negative on other relation or property field names in the same position ("award",
"origin", "birth", "label", "cast", "genre", ...). Used as a plain word ("the country",
"our country") it is near zero. It is mildly positive on a few reading-comprehension and
question words ("speaker", "name", "What", "How", "Why", "mentions").

Everything else is predicted as the typical activation, about 0.03.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Tokens that open a field in a list of facts (e.g. "Name -> field -> value").
SEPARATORS = {"->", "|", ":", ",", "—", "):"}

# Property names that label a field of an entity record.
FIELD_NAMES = {
    "country", "award", "origin", "label", "birth", "citizenship", "genre", "languages",
    "language", "cast", "director", "performer", "father", "mother", "parent", "child",
    "sibling", "composer", "author", "sport", "team", "member", "party", "position",
    "family", "employer", "record", "occupation", "spouse", "founder", "location",
    "nationality", "religion", "instrument",
}

# Mild positive words in reading-comprehension and question text.
POSITIVE_WORDS = {"speaker": 0.85, "name": 0.47, "What": 0.43, "How": 0.41, "Why": 0.36,
                  "mentions": 0.5, "born": 0.47, "located": 0.34}

BASELINE = 0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() if len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 else ""
    if word in FIELD_NAMES and before in SEPARATORS:
        value = -3.0 if word == "country" else -1.2
    elif word in POSITIVE_WORDS:
        value = POSITIVE_WORDS[word]
    else:
        value = BASELINE
    return carry, value

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 2190, the unit this component reads out, goes negative on the
word that follows a noun and attaches it to a predicate or modifier: the copula or auxiliary
after a subject ("the system [is]", "the file [was]", "the tool [can]"), a relative word after
a noun ("a valve [which]", "the rule [that]"), a preposition or bracket after a noun, and most
strongly the case and topic particles of Japanese and Korean ("を", "が", "は", "이", "을").
After a pronoun ("it is") the copula is near zero, so the rule looks at the word before.

Program: if the current token is a particle, it gets that particle's typical value. If it is a
linking word or punctuation and the previous token is a content word (a letters-only token that
is not a function word), it gets that word's typical value. Everything else predicts 0. This
explains only a few percent of the variance: most of the activation depends on context that
is not a word list.
"""

import regex

READS = ()

# Typical activation of a word that follows a content word (corpus means).
AFTER_NOUN = {
    " is": -2.0, " was": -2.2, " are": -1.6, " were": -1.3, " which": -2.2, " that": -1.0,
    " can": -1.2, " will": -1.0, " has": -0.9, " have": -0.4, " may": -0.8, " would": -0.8,
    " such": -1.3, " including": -1.3, " called": -1.9, " who": -1.0, " for": -0.6, " as": -0.5,
    " in": -0.4, " from": -0.4, " at": -0.45, " on": -0.4, " (": -1.3, "'s": -0.6, " =": -0.6,
    ":": -0.3, ",": -0.3,
}

# Case, topic and possessive particles that follow a noun phrase in Japanese, Korean, Chinese.
PARTICLES = {
    "を": -4.1, "が": -3.6, "は": -2.7, "も": -2.7, "に": -2.1, "の": -1.7, "的": -1.1,
    "です": -2.4, "이": -2.7, "을": -3.6, "를": -3.8,
}

# Pronouns, articles, conjunctions, prepositions and auxiliaries: not content words.
FUNCTION_WORDS = {
    "it", "he", "she", "they", "we", "i", "you", "this", "that", "these", "those", "which", "who",
    "what", "there", "here", "the", "a", "an", "and", "or", "but", "of", "in", "to", "for", "with",
    "on", "at", "by", "from", "as", "is", "was", "are", "were", "be", "been", "being", "not",
    "also", "so", "if", "when", "then", "than", "its", "their", "his", "her", "our", "my", "your",
    "all", "some", "no", "can", "will", "has", "have", "had", "do", "does", "did", "may", "would",
}


def is_content_word(token):
    """A letters-only token, with an optional leading space, that is not a function word."""
    if not regex.fullmatch(r"\s?\p{L}+", token):
        return False
    return token.strip().lower() not in FUNCTION_WORDS

breaks. It is a rough summary: most of its variation depends on context this program
does not model.

  value = -5.5 + 1.35 * log2(position) + 1.8 * log2(1 + copy_length)

import unicodedata

MAX_COPY = 64        # longest copy length counted
MAX_CANDIDATES = 64  # earlier occurrences of the current token searched


def token_kind(text):
    """Coarse kind of a token's text: 'digit', 'symbol', 'newline' or 'other'."""
    if text.strip() == "":

    toks.append(token)
    copy_len = 0  # length of the run of latest tokens that repeats an earlier run
    for j in seen.get(token, [])[-MAX_CANDIDATES:]:

    if t in ("'t", "’t") and prev in NEG_BE:

"""Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:2227, read as a small token-class readout.

What the component is: its input direction is mostly MLP hidden unit 2227 of layer 15
(about 0.78 of its norm), so its activation is roughly that neuron's value times 0.77.
The neuron is noisy and heavy-tailed (kurtosis about 12) and is driven by context that no
token-level rule captured: knowing the current token explains about 1% of its variance,
the previous token nothing, and its causal importance is essentially 0, so zeroing it
barely changes the model.

What this program does: it predicts a small value from the kind of token at each position,
the only coarse pattern with a consistent sign:
  - chat and reasoning markers (<|endoftext|>, <|im_start|>, <think>, ...) are positive;
  - whitespace-only and punctuation-only tokens are mildly positive;
  - digits are slightly positive; other tokens are close to zero;
  - the first token of a row, and the first token of each document inside a packed row,
    are exactly 0, as the model's attention-sink positions are.
It explains almost none of the variance. It is a description of the component's weak
average tendencies, not of what drives its large swings.
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Chat-template and reasoning-trace markers.
MARKERS = {
    "<|endoftext|>",
    "<|im_start|>",
    "<|im_end|>",
    "<think>",
    "</think>",
    "<tool_call>",
    "</tool_call>",
}


def token_class(text: str) -> str:
    """Coarse class of one token's text: space, punctuation, digits, or other."""
    if text.strip() == "":
        return "space"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*[^\w\s]+\s*", text):
        return "punct"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s*\d+", text):
        return "digit"
    return "other"


# Mean activation by class, from about 4 million training positions.
CLASS_MEAN = {"space": 0.07, "punct": 0.07, "digit": 0.04, "other": 0.02}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # The first token of a row, or of a document inside a packed row, gives exactly 0.
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return carry, 0.0
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if text in MARKERS:
        return carry, 0.3
    return carry, CLASS_MEAN[token_class(text)]

2230), so its value is that unit's activation, scaled. The value is diffuse: it varies a lot
from token to token, but token identity, the neighbouring tokens, and simple structural
features (brackets, quotes, indentation, repetition, position) predict it only weakly, under
1% of its variance on held-out text. The one clear, readable pattern is the `grep` command:
the value is large on the word `grep` and on the next few tokens of the command (its flags,
such as `-A 5`, and the start of the pattern), and fades out after about eight tokens. The
rest of the time this program predicts 0, so it captures only that pattern (about 0.8% of
the variance); the large values elsewhere, in code and prose, are not explained here.

Rule, counted in tokens since the last `grep` in the same document:
  0 (the `grep` token itself)  -> 4.0
  1 (the token right after it) -> 0
  2 to 4                       -> 2.0
  5 to 8                       -> 0.5
  otherwise, or no grep yet    -> 0

"""

GREP = "grep"
# tokens since the last `grep` -> predicted activation
PROFILE = {0: 4.0, 2: 2.0, 3: 2.0, 4: 2.0, 5: 0.5, 6: 0.5, 7: 0.5, 8: 0.5}

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 2231 (this component reads almost only that unit).

It fires on ordinary words written inside mathematical research prose. On each
alphabetic word token it predicts 10 times a density: an exponential average,
over the earlier tokens of the same document, of how often a token is a
proof/theorem word (theorem, lemma, proof, prove, conjecture, assume, suppose,
hold, bounded, ...). The density resets at each new document. Punctuation,
digits, code and LaTeX symbols are predicted as 0.
This captures about 1.3% of the activation's variance (r = 0.12 on eval): the
rest is set by context the rule does not see."""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

PROOF_WORDS = {
    "theorem", "theorems", "lemma", "lemmas", "proof", "proofs", "prove", "proves", "proved",
    "conjecture", "bounded", "function", "functions", "assume", "assumption", "paper", "results",
    "result", "exists", "satisfies", "constant", "factor", "fixed", "hold", "holds", "verified",
    "extend", "show", "shown", "suppose", "define", "defined", "denote", "theory", "space",
    "spaces", "prime", "integer", "integers", "finite", "infinite", "set", "sets",
}
DECAY = 0.99
SCALE = 10.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    density, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, None)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != last_doc:
        density = 0.0
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    is_word = text.isalpha()
    value = SCALE * density if is_word else 0.0
    is_proof_word = 1.0 if text.lower() in PROOF_WORDS else 0.0
    density = DECAY * density + (1 - DECAY) * is_proof_word
    return (density, doc), value

"""Layer 15, MLP hidden unit 2235: a code-reading unit, written into the residual by the component.

What it does, in plain terms. The unit is silent in prose and active in code. Its sign
depends on the role of the current token in the code:

  * positive on the name (or return type) of a function or method being declared, e.g.
    the "Add" of "public void Add(", the "New" of "func New(", the "Load" after "err :=";
    positive too on the keyword that starts a declaration ("public", "void", "func", "def")
    and on doc-comment markers (" *", "///", "@", "param");
  * negative on the first word of a statement inside a function body: "this", "self",
    "return", "$this" at the start of a line.

Outside code (few brackets, braces or sigils in the last 16 tokens) the signal is damped
by 0.3. Activations persist over several tokens, so the per-token values are folded into a
running average (decay 0.7) that is reset at each document boundary.

This is a rough explanation. It captures about 2% of the variance: the unit's large values
sit on many different identifiers in code, and no short rule separates them. A lookup of the
current token would reach about 4% and is not a concept, so it is left out.
"""
import re

READS = ()

DECL_KEYWORDS = {"public", "private", "protected", "static", "void", "def", "func", "fn",
                 "function", "pub", "async", "int", "bool", "string", "String"}
BODY_WORDS = {"this", "self", "return", "$this"}
DOC_MARKERS = {"*", "///", "@", "param"}
CODE_SYMBOLS = re.compile(r"[{};()=<>\[\]$@]")
DECAY = 0.7
SCALE = 1.2


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_row = carry is None or prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_row:
        carry = {"prev": "", "line": "", "symbols": [], "avg": 0.0}
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = s.strip()
    recent = carry["symbols"][-16:]
    in_code = sum(recent) / max(1, len(recent)) > 0.1
    if word in BODY_WORDS and carry["line"].strip() in ("", word):
        value = -2.0
    elif carry["prev"] in DECL_KEYWORDS and re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_]\w*", word):
        value = 4.0
    elif word in DECL_KEYWORDS or word in DOC_MARKERS:
        value = 2.0
    else:
        value = 0.0
    if not in_code:
        value *= 0.3
    carry["avg"] = DECAY * carry["avg"] + (1 - DECAY) * value
    carry["symbols"].append(bool(CODE_SYMBOLS.search(s)))
    carry["line"] = s.split("\n")[-1] if "\n" in s else carry["line"] + s
    carry["prev"] = word
    return carry, SCALE * carry["avg"]

"""Copy-continuation detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 2236.

This component is near zero on ordinary text and turns clearly negative when the
current token continues a phrase that already appeared earlier in the same document.
The more tokens of the phrase that repeat (the current token, the one before it, and
so on, back to the earlier copy), the more negative it gets. A single repeated token
is roughly neutral, and a copy of three or more tokens in a row is clearly negative.

The program tracks each document's tokens. At each position it finds the earlier
occurrence of the current token that matches the longest run of preceding tokens
(the "match length" M, counting the current token). It predicts
    -0.6 * min(max(M - 2, 0), 6)
so a match of 3 tokens gives -0.6, and 8 or more tokens give about -3.6.
"""

READS = ()

STEP = 0.6  # activation units per extra matched token
FIRST = 2  # matches up to this length are neutral
CAP = 6  # matched tokens beyond FIRST that still add to the effect
MAX_RUN = 12  # longest run checked backwards, enough to reach the cap


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        carry = {"doc": prefix.document_ids[-1], "ids": [], "where": {}}
    ids = carry["ids"]
    where = carry["where"]
    tok = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    i = len(ids)
    ids.append(tok)
    # longest run of tokens ending here that matches an earlier run ending at some j
    best = 0
    for j in where.get(tok, []):
        run = 1
        while run < MAX_RUN and j - run >= 0 and ids[j - run] == ids[i - run]:
            run += 1
        best = max(best, run)
    where.setdefault(tok, []).append(i)
    value = -STEP * min(max(best - FIRST, 0), CAP)
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 2237: a weak, mostly negative signal on
identifiers in source code.

Plain terms: the component sits near a small negative baseline on most tokens. It goes
negative on programming names (variables, fields, functions and parameters such as
`value`, `node`, `self`, `err`, `_id`). It is most negative when the name is inside a
call's parentheses, where a value is being handed to a function, and when the token
itself fuses an opening parenthesis with a name, like `(self` or `($`, and tokens that
are just an opening parenthesis, like `(` or `((`, are negative too. camelCase and
snake_case names are more negative still. Ordinary prose tokens sit near zero.

The program keeps only the parenthesis depth of the text so far (reset at each document
start) and reads the current token's characters. It is a linear fit of a few such
features, so it captures only a small part of the variance.
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Leading punctuation or spaces that can come before a name inside a token.
LEAD = "([{ ,.$!&*+-=\\'\"\t\n"
NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
CAMEL_OR_SNAKE = re.compile(r"[a-z][A-Z]|_")

# Least-squares means fitted on sampled training positions.
BASE = -0.07          # a typical position
IN_CALL_NAME = -0.38  # a name inside parentheses
NAME_CAMEL = -0.43    # a camelCase or snake_case name
PAREN_NAME = -0.53    # a token that fuses "(" with a name, e.g. "(self"
PAREN_ONLY = -0.5     # a token that is an opening parenthesis with no name, e.g. "(" or "(("


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # carry: (open parenthesis depth before this token, document of the last token)
    depth, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else (0, None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != last_doc:
        depth = 0  # a new document starts with nothing open
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    core = token.lstrip(LEAD)
    is_name = NAME.fullmatch(core) is not None

    value = BASE
    if is_name:
        if depth > 0:
            value += IN_CALL_NAME
        if CAMEL_OR_SNAKE.search(core):
            value += NAME_CAMEL
        if token.startswith("("):
            value += PAREN_NAME
    elif token.startswith("("):
        value += PAREN_ONLY

    opened = token.count("(") + token.count("[") + token.count("{")
    closed = token.count(")") + token.count("]") + token.count("}")
    depth = max(0, depth + opened - closed)
    return (depth, prefix.document_ids[-1]), value

"""Predicts the activation of Qwen3-1.7B layer 15's MLP down_proj component 2238.

What it does: this component has no interpretable trigger. Its activation is a
diffuse linear readout of the MLP's hidden units (its largest single weight is on
hidden unit 2238, but that unit alone correlates only 0.29 with it), and it shows
no dependence on the current token's identity, its character class, or the token
before it. The one regularity found is positional: within a document, the first
few tokens (roughly positions 2 to 19) average slightly positive, and later tokens
average about zero. This program predicts that position-dependent mean and nothing
else. It is a readable description of what is weakly predictable, not a model of
the component's computation; it explains only about 0.1% of the activation's variance.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation by token position within a document (measured on training rows).
EARLY_MEAN = {0: 0.0, 1: 0.0, 2: 0.12, 3: 0.09, 4: 0.09}
MID_MEAN = 0.05      # positions 5-9
NEAR_MEAN = 0.03     # positions 10-19
LATE_MEAN = -0.01    # positions 20 and later


def _position_mean(p):
    if p in EARLY_MEAN:
        return EARLY_MEAN[p]
    if p < 10:
        return MID_MEAN
    if p < 20:
        return NEAR_MEAN
    return LATE_MEAN


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label of the previous token, its position in the document)
    if carry is None or prefix.document_ids[-1] != carry[0]:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    return (prefix.document_ids[-1], pos), _position_mean(pos)

"""Limiter detector: layers.15.mlp.down_proj, component 2239.

What it does: this component writes a strongly negative value at words that mean
"merely / no more than", above all "only" and "just" (also "simply", "merely", and
their translations: nur, solo, apenas, hanya, seulement, tylko, csak, 仅, 只, のみ,
только). It is weaker on words that restrict a quantity ("single", "few", "handful",
"sole", "alone", "simple"). Right after a limiter it is mildly negative ("only a", "just one"). Where the limiter negates or
compares ("not only", "than just") the value is nearly switched off; after "the"
("the only ...") it is about 60% of normal. Everywhere else it is 0.

Why: the activation sign and size track how exclusive the word is. Most of the
variance sits on "only" and "just" (about a third of it), so a word table with a
few context rules captures most of the component's behaviour.

Scope: this is a readable approximation. It ignores the within-context spread
(e.g. "is only" about -35, "the only" about -14), which a word table cannot
capture.
"""

READS = ()

# Activation at the limiting word itself.
LIMITER = {
    " only": -23, " Only": -25, "only": -23, " ONLY": -10,
    " just": -18, " Just": -14, "just": -13,
    " merely": -17, " simply": -15, " Simply": -14, " solely": -12, " purely": -10,
    " barely": -15, " mere": -10,
    " nur": -21, " Nur": -18, " solo": -20, " apenas": -31, " hanya": -32,
    " seulement": -11, " seul": -11, " seule": -13, " tylko": -12, " csak": -15, " bara": -13,
    "仅": -31, "只": -18, "只有": -22, "只是": -17, "只要": -14, "唯一": -12,
    "のみ": -21, " только": -17, " лишь": -29,
}

# Quantity words that restrict ("a single", "a few", "alone").
QUANTITY = {" single": -7, " few": -7, " handful": -9, " sole": -7, " alone": -4.5, " simple": -4}

NEGATING = {" not", " Not", " than"}      # "not only", "than just": switched nearly off


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else None

    if token in LIMITER:
        value = LIMITER[token]
        if before in NEGATING:
            value *= 0.1
        elif before in {" the", "The"}:
            value *= 0.6
        return carry, float(value)
    if token in QUANTITY:
        return carry, float(QUANTITY[token])
    if before in LIMITER:
        return carry, -4.0  # the word right after "only" / "just": "only a", "just one"
    return carry, 0.0
